items.text: Adults 21 and over may possess, buy and carry up to 28.5 g of cannabis and 8 g of concentrate, and grow up to 6 plants at home. Use is allowed on private property (owners can ban it) but not in public places or anywhere tobacco smoking is banned, nor within 1,000 feet of a school, day care or youth centre while children are present. Most hotels ban it; check local city or county rules. Federal land (national parks) and crossing state lines remain illegal.

laws.rule: Adults 21 and over may possess up to 28.5 g of cannabis and 8 g of concentrate under state law (Health and Safety Code 11362.1). Consumption is allowed only on private property where the owner permits it; not in public, in vehicles, on federal land, or within 1,000 feet of a school, daycare or youth centre while children are present. Cannabis remains illegal under US federal law.
Muir Woods National Monument: pets are not allowed on any trail or in ranger programs.

San Francisco's Police Code bans drinking alcohol on public streets, sidewalks and other public property open to public view (Police Code section 21). Its Park Code (section 4.10) bans alcohol in park buildings, children's play areas, pools, restrooms and a list of named parks unless the Recreation and Park Department gives permission, and section 4.11 lets park staff and police exclude intoxicated people.
laws.penalty_signal: infraction, fine reported as US$25 to US$100 (about A$36 to A$142 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026)

laws.rule: San Francisco's Health Code (section 1009.81) prohibits smoking in unenclosed City park and recreation areas, with signs posted.

Los Angeles County beaches (which include Venice, Dockweiler and Manhattan Beach) post these rules: no alcoholic beverages, no smoking, no glass containers, no fires or barbecues, no animals of any kind, and no loitering between midnight and 6 am. The county's permit paperwork says no alcohol permits are issued for Venice, Dockweiler, Manhattan, Redondo or Torrance beaches. The page lists no penalties.

sites.name: Mount Shasta Wilderness
sites.what: Volcano in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest visited by over 100,000 people a year for cultural, spiritual and physical pursuits (USFS).

access.permits: Free wilderness permit for everyone, year round; Summit Pass above 10,000 ft USD 25 (3 days) or USD 30 annual; groups of 10 or fewer; no dogs; stay on trails; pack out human waste
access.closures: Forest Order 14-24-08 runs to 8 November 2026; recheck for a renewal

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Yosemite National Park
layers.process: For 2026 Yosemite states that no reservation is needed to enter the park; the entrance fee still applies. The park chose not to run a season-wide timed-entry system and plans traffic monitoring and parking management instead. Rules can change, so the park's conditions page is the live source.

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Yosemite National Park
layers.process: Half Dome beyond the base of the subdome needs a permit on every day the cables are up (normally the Friday before Memorial Day to the day after the second Monday in October; subject to conditions). Up to 300 hikers a day: about 225 day hikers and 75 backpackers. Preseason lottery: apply 1 to 31 March, results in mid-April, up to six permits per application. Daily lottery: apply from midnight to 4 pm Pacific two days before. Fees: US$10 (about A$14) per application, non-refundable, and US$10 per person if issued. The page does not list 2026 calendar dates; confirm on recreation.gov. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.

layers.authority: USDA Forest Service, Inyo National Forest (via recreation.gov)
layers.process: A wilderness permit is required year-round for the Mt Whitney Trail and Whitney Zone, for day use or overnight. Lottery results post on 15 March; awarded permits must be claimed and paid by 21 April; unclaimed dates reopen on 22 April. Fees: US$6 per reservation, non-refundable, and US$15 (about A$21) per person for the Whitney Zone. Day-use permits are valid midnight to midnight and must be printed by noon the day before, or they count as a no-show. No refunds. The page gives this as the annual schedule, not 2026 dates; confirm with the Inyo permit office, 760-873-2526. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Yosemite National Park
layers.process: A wilderness permit is required year-round for backpacking, overnight climbing or any overnight stay in the wilderness (not for day hikes, except Half Dome). Late April to October, reservations are required: 60 per cent of each trailhead's daily quota is released by lottery 24 weeks ahead, and 40 per cent 7 days ahead. Unreserved permits on the start day are few, if any. Wilderness centres open 8 am to 5 pm. In winter, permits are issued the day before or the day of. Fees were not on the page read. Food must be stored properly, and bear canisters can be rented at the Valley Welcome Center. The page was last updated 31 December 2025. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Muir Woods National Monument
layers.process: Parking and shuttle reservations are required for all visitors, vehicle or shuttle rider, and booked at GoMuirWoods.com (separate from the entrance fee). Entrance: US$15 per person aged 16 and over (about A$21.30); the Annual Pass (US$45) is for US citizens and residents. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
